text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malaysia Deputy Home Affairs Megat Junid Megat Ayub says East Timor meeting organisers and demonstrators will face charges in court.
- United States show restraint in settling trade conflicts with other nations under World Trade Organisation.
- Australian Prime Minister John Howard tells Australians to accept Kuala Lumpur actions on break up of conference on East Timor.
- Cable & Wireless plc in talks with Global One on large-scale international co-operation in phone industry.
- Japan unveils moves to make financial system freer, fairer and more global by 2001.
- China Strategic Holdings Ltd Chairman Oei Hong Leong raises bid for investment company to Hong Kong $2.80 a share from $2.50 a share, valuing company at Hong Kong $1.85 billion.
- Singapore Institute of Surveyors and Valuers data shows Indonesians biggest foreign buyers of residential property in Singapore, followed by Malaysians and Hongkongers.
- U.S.-patented technology, Soft Audio, developed by Colarado-based CD-ROM Inc, looking for home in Singapore.
- Initial public offer investors more selective and looking at company fundamentals and issue details.
- Brierley Investments Ltd could invest at least New Zealand $1 billion in the next 12 months in new investment opportunities.
- Malayan Banking Bhd and Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd have jointly developed an index to track property market's performance.
- LC Development might sell its 35% stake in Solarvest.
